the small heat shock protein HSPB1 selectively interacts with and promotes the degradation of three distinct mutant forms of the small heat shock chaperone CryAB.

the overexpression or knockdown of the small heat shock protein HSPB1 (HSP27) affects the solubilization, stability, and clearance of the three structurally-distict CryAB mutants, R120G, delA and delCT, by the ubiquitin proteasome system.
HSPB1 interacts selectively with three structurally-distinc CryAB mutants and mediates their selective clearance through the UPS.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular mechanisms underlying the clearance of mutant sHSPs, a key process in the pathophysiology of sHSP-related inherited myofibril disorders.
the role of HSPB in selective clearance of CryAB mutant proteins and the potential role of proteasomal degradation of mutant proteins in myofibrillatory disorders.
the molecular mechanisms of the sHSPs and their role in the pathogenesis of myofibrillopathies.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
HSPB1 selectively degrades CryAB mutants via the UPS, and this selective degradation might be important to the pathogenesis of the disease and its potential treatment.
HSPB1 can selectively interact with CryAB mutants, and such interactions are critical for the solubility stability and degradation of aggregation prone CryAB mutants.
HSPB1 plays a critical role in regulating the solubility/stability of CryAB mutants, which may have important implications for clinical manifestation and potential therapeutic approaches.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
HSPB1 selectively degrades the aggregation-prone CryA mutants by the UPS.
the selective clearance of aggregate-prone mutant proteins by HSPB may be an effective therapeutic approach to treat myofibrillatory myopathies.

the selective degradation of aggregation-pronemutants of sHSPs by HSPB is mediated by the UPS.
